quotes.text: DiagBench integrates data from four distinct sources: MIMIC-IV [ 18 ] , PMC-OA case reports [ 19 ]

rationale: The four source datasets are named with citations and access links, and PMC-OA cases are bounded by a publication date. No MIMIC-IV version or snapshot is given and no route from a benchmark case back to its source record is documented, so 1.

quotes.text: The data source for this work is MIMIC-IV. Due to licensing restrictions, we are unable to directly open-source the dataset.

rationale: Origin (MIMIC-IV, PMC-OA, MTSamples, DDXPlus), construction pipeline and a licensing restriction are stated. Consent or IRB status, or an explicit not-required statement, is absent, so 1.

quotes.text: we perform stratified random sampling across all four data sources in DiagBench, selecting 100 clinical cases from each center

rationale: A sampling design (stratified by source, disease-wise sampling) and descriptive case counts are given. The paper only notes possible ED/ICU bias and does not compare against a named target population, so 1.
searched: S1 (paper, results, limitations, appendix), S2 (README), S3 (none), S4 and S5 (eval code and prompts). No dedicated unsafe-output test or bias test is reported.

quotes.text: To rigorously prevent data leakage and assess generalization on unseen data, we strictly selected case reports published after January 2025.

rationale: A developer-side control exists: a temporal cutoff for PMC-OA cases plus a train/test split for MIMIC-IV. No measured overlap or contamination check is reported, so 1.

quotes.text: unlike \mathcal{B} in the environment model, contains no information about the final diagnosis

rationale: The paper states that the agent state (initial inquiry plus examination history) excludes the final diagnosis, which only the simulator profile holds. No run-time isolation mechanism (no mount, no credential, no network path) is named, so 1.

quotes.text: LLM-as-a-judge (GPT-4o, version gpt-4o-2024-08-06)

rationale: The judge snapshot, simulator model release and software versions (vllm==0.8.3) are partly pinned, but evaluation depends on a live GPT-4o API judge and a served simulator, and the DiagBench data version is not pinned. The eval code defaults to the unpinned alias gpt-4o, which is a candidate contradiction with the pinned snapshot in the paper.

quotes.text: To ensure clinical validity, each case undergoes a rigorous review by a physician.

rationale: Only manual evidence is given: a physician reviews each case and its reference trajectory. No scripted reference solution is run through the grader and the result reported, so 1.

searched: S1 (problem formulation, evaluation settings), S2, S4/S5 (inference code). Tasks are diagnostic information gathering and a final diagnosis; simulated examination results only extend the history, and no task changes environment state that a grader could check for side effects.

searched: S1 (results, ablations, appendix tables), S2 (README results), S3 (none), S4/S5. No random or trivial-agent rate, chance rate per metric, or design argument against trivial success is given. Zero-shot LLM baselines are not a trivial agent.
searched: S1 (all results tables), S2 (README tables), S3 (none), S4/S5. No do-nothing or random agent score is reported for any task.

quotes.text: the LLM achieved near-perfect alignment with the human consensus (e.g., 100.00% for Diagnosis Accuracy and 96.00% for Rubric Hit Ratio)

rationale: The benchmark validates its own GPT-4o judge against three-physician consensus on 100 sampled instances per metric, with agreement percentages and an MAE for counting. Supplementary Table 1 reports figures, including a low 62% agreement for one physician on the rubric metric.

quotes.text: def __init__(self, model_name_or_path, max_tokens=8192, temperature=0.0) -> None:

rationale: Temperature 0 appears in the README example, and judge calls use temperature 0 in README/code (seed=42 in the RL README). No repeated-run policy is stated and the DiagGym simulator is sampled at temperature 1.0, so safeguards are partial.

quotes.text: Error bars show 95% confidence intervals. Significance levels relative to the DiagAgent-14B are marked as:

rationale: Tables carry 95% CIs and the figures mark significance levels (p<0.05, 0.01, 0.001) relative to DiagAgent-14B for the headline comparison with baselines. The specific test is not named.

quotes.text: max_tokens=8192, temperature=0.0

rationale: Decoding controls (temperature 0.0, max_tokens) are shown in the README example. The number of runs per task behind each headline score and run independence are not stated.

quotes.text: All metrics are reported with 95% Confidence Intervals

rationale: 95% CIs are given on headline results. The resampling unit (case versus turn, single-turn expands 750 cases to 4,485 turns) is not named and clustering of turns within cases is not addressed.
searched: S1 (results, appendix), S2 (README), S3 (none), S4/S5. No repeat-run, action-level, state-level or pass^k reliability information is reported.

quotes.text: max_tokens=8192, temperature=0.0

rationale: Decoding parameters appear in README usage code. Element (i) counts as absent: the paper pins gpt-4o-2024-08-06 but the eval code uses the alias gpt-4o, and Claude is given as claude-sonnet-4 with release years that differ between paper and README. No harness tag or commit is tied to the reported numbers; only a vllm==0.8.3 dependency pin.

quotes.text: The available information is sufficient to make a diagnosis. Diagnosis: [Diagnosis result] Reason: [Diagnosis reason]

rationale: The agent uses a text-command protocol (not NA) with a fixed response format given in Prompt 5. Side effects per action are not documented and the simulator's return semantics, including failures, are not specified; only the format element is present.

quotes.text: While the assessment necessarily relies on the external diagnostics world model to simulate examination results

rationale: The paper discloses that examination results are simulated by DiagGym. No conformance tests of the action or return protocol are reported, and the agent-visible prompt does not say results are simulated.

quotes.text: allowing the diagnostic agents to order tests and immediately observe their consequences
and computing precision, recall, and F1-score to measure recommendation quality

rationale: Examination recommendations are simulated clinical orders, so the item applies. Simulation of results is disclosed and unneeded orders lower precision, F1 and a turn-based reward. The paper does not say which actions write or are irreversible, and the simulation status is not in the agent prompt.

quotes.text: To avoid issues with synonyms and the inclusion relationships between examinations, we utilize GPT-4o to judge

rationale: Grader inputs are named (answer strings and the trajectory judged by GPT-4o against rubrics) and a rationale is given for LLM judging. The human validation reports overall agreement on 100 instances per metric but no per-class error rates, so element (iii) is not met.

quotes.text: prevent leakage of the final diagnosis into the initial inquiry, we applied a two-stage filtering process

rationale: Leakage into the agent-visible initial inquiry is filtered. Benchmark cases and rubrics are publicly released, so no held-out private labels exist, and no canary or provenance marker is reported.

quotes.text: In-Domain | MIMIC-IV [ 18 ] | [Link] | Critical Care and Emergency Medicine | 750 | 973

rationale: Results are reported per data source, per in-domain versus out-of-domain split and per evaluation setting, with case counts per slice. No results per patient subgroup are given although the source records hold demographic fields.

quotes.text: Due to licensing restrictions, we are unable to directly open-source the processed dataset.
which will be made publicly available on PhysioNet upon approval

rationale: Records are stated to derive from MIMIC-IV EHRs, with DDXPlus labelled synthesized (generator not named). Credentialing is stated (CITI certification, PhysioNet approval), and data terms are given apart from the code. De-identification method and IRB status are not stated.
